subject: Re: EuropaHealth — scoped debug-trace escrow and retention scope
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@europahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: EuropaHealth Security Team <security@europahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Scoped retention request — debug traces for tenant EU-7789

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. We have an ongoing need from our Incident Response team to preserve a restricted set of debug traces for one tenant (EU-7789) for a limited window after operational incidents. The ask is: retain encrypted debug traces (stack traces + correlation IDs) for 90 days instead of the default 30-day ephemeral window so our forensic team can complete regulatory audits in certain EU jurisdictions.

We know this is atypical — we do not need full request/response payloads or customer PII, just the debug trace blobs and associated metadata (timestamp, tenant id, correlation id). EuropaHealth is preparing a short justification and regulatory citation for the 90-day request (attached is a PSA and an initial scope spreadsheet). Can Redwood provide:

- A proposed scope describing exactly what will be retained vs deleted
- A technical approach for escrowing those traces (encryption-at-rest, key handling, access logging)
- SOC 2 / CAIQ artifacts that demonstrate controls around time-limited retention and secure deletion
- ETA for evidence and whether an exception can be scoped to the tenant only (not org-wide)

We're on a tight audit timeline (audit kickoff July 5). Happy to jump on a short call if useful.

Attachments: europa_psa.pdf, requested-scope.xlsx

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Security Operations | EuropaHealth

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@europahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Scoped retention request — debug traces for tenant EU-7789

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. I've looped in Karthik (security) and Irene (legal/compliance) so we can scope this properly and give you the artifacts you need for the audit. A couple quick clarifying questions to help us draft a scoped proposal:

1) Can you confirm tenant identifier(s) and whether this applies to production only?
2) You mention "stack traces + correlation IDs" — can you confirm no request/response bodies or embeddings are required to be retained?
3) Will EuropaHealth provide a written legal/regulatory justification we can include with our exception ticket? (you referenced one in your note)
4) Do you require Redwood-managed key escrow or will you use your own KMS with a BYOK arrangement?

Assuming answers align with the minimal scope you described, we can propose a tenant-scoped conditional retention policy: encrypted container for debug traces, 90-day TTL, automated verification and deletion job with signed proof-of-delete artifacts, and restricted RBAC + audit logging. We will also map the approach to relevant CAIQ sections and SOC 2 control descriptions.

Irene/Karthik — initial ask attached (europa_psa.pdf and requested-scope.xlsx). If we can agree on a narrow technical definition, I propose we prepare:
- A compact evidence packet for EuropaHealth (CAIQ pointers + SOC 2 control excerpts)
- Implementation plan (retention flagging, encrypted escrow, deletion verification)
- A short customer-facing carveout addendum for the contract (tenant-scoped, time-limited)

I can turn this into a ticket and target a vendor response by 2026-06-23 so EuropaHealth has time before July 5. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Security | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@europahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Scoped retention request — debug traces for tenant EU-7789

Lauren — thanks. Answers inline:

1) Tenant: EU-7789 (production only).
2) Correct — no request/response payloads, no embeddings, no user PII. Only crash/exception traces and correlation ids needed.
3) Attached is a short justification (europa_psa.pdf) and the requested-scope.xlsx shows the fields we need.
4) EuropaHealth prefers Redwood-managed escrow for speed, but we can consider BYOK if Redwood requires it for compliance.

We definitely need the evidence packet mapped to CAIQ (control IDs would be helpful) and a deletion attestation that we can present to auditors. If you can target a draft by 06/23 that would be ideal. We can do a 30-minute call Friday if that helps.

Thanks,
Marta

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@europahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 14:46:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Scoped retention request — debug traces for tenant EU-7789

Folks — looping back with proposed approach and open items. Draft below; I'll flag where we need legal sign-off.

Proposed technical scope (tenant EU-7789, prod only):
- Data retained: exception stack traces (text blobs), correlation_id, timestamp, tenant_id. Explicitly excluded: request/response payloads, prompt/embeddings, user PII.
- Storage: encrypted object container with envelope encryption (Redwood-managed KMS). Per-tenant namespace and access isolation.
- TTL: 90 days from trace ingestion; automated background job purges objects and generates a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 list + timestamp) stored in immutable audit storage for 365 days for audit trail.
- Access controls: RBAC: SRE-on-call read-only via just-in-time access; access requires an approved incident ticket and is logged.
- Evidence: map to CAIQ sections: Data Retention (CC-DR-03), Access Controls (CC-AC-02), Key Management (CC-KM-01). We'll extract SOC 2 control text excerpts and produce a 1-page mapping doc.

Open items for Irene/legal:
- Customer carveout language: tenant-scoped exception addendum (time-limited, closes after last retention purge). Need sign-off on wording and whether BYOK must be mandatory for EU customers.
- Export / transfer: confirm there are no cross-border retention implications for Redwood-managed keys (we may need to note data residency - all objects will remain in eu-west-1).

Operational notes:
- We should add a short QA step: before purge, run a verification job that confirms TTL and that no excluded payloads are present. That helps reduce audit disputes.
- Attach retention-playbook-v2.docx with implementation checklist; I will open a secure ticket (RDW-4531) and target 2026-06-23 for the evidence packet.

If Irene signs off, I recommend we send EuropaHealth a concise proposal and the CAIQ mapping tomorrow.

— Karthik
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
